source: MAFF/JICA APPP (Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap) Farmer Field School Technical Manual for Extension Officers, December 2014 -- no elibrary URL visible on this scan.
province: Battambang, Pursat, Kampong Chhnang (APPP project area)
text: Before rice seed (ពកូជស្រូវ) is stored or planted, farmers can separate high-quality, fully-filled seed from empty or poor seed using a salt-water floating test (ការដោមោឃទិន្នផលននការពូជ). Add salt gradually to about 10 liters of water while stirring, and check the strength of the solution with a fresh egg (សួតរស្ស): keep adding salt until the egg floats with a small, coin-sized patch showing above the water surface -- that is roughly the right salinity for testing paddy seed. Pour the rice seed into this salt solution and stir well. Empty or poorly-filled seed will float to the surface and should be skimmed off and discarded; the seed that sinks is fuller and heavier and should be kept for planting. Rinse the selected seed thoroughly in clean water afterward, since leftover salt on the seed coat can harm germination. After selection, disinfect the seed by soaking it in hot water held at about 60 degrees Celsius for about 10 minutes -- no longer, and not hotter, since excessive heat can kill the seed embryo. This hot-water soak step helps control some seed-borne diseases before sowing.
caveat: The source gives approximate salt (or urea) amounts per 10 liters of water for building test solutions of different strengths -- roughly 1.1 kg salt for a 'medium' density solution and roughly 2 kg salt for a 'high' density solution (with somewhat higher amounts if urea is used instead of salt). These figures come from a scanned training table and should be treated as a rough starting point rather than an exact recipe; the simplest, most reliable field method remains the fresh-egg buoyancy check described above.
